news.title: Full year 2026 earnings released: EPS: ₹3.85 (vs ₹2.29 in FY 2025)
news.body: Full year 2026 results: EPS: ₹3.85 (up from ₹2.29 in FY 2025). Revenue: ₹1.09b (up 23% from FY 2025). Net income: ₹19.2m (up 68% from FY 2025). Profit margin: 1.8% (up from 1.3% in FY 2025). The increase in margin was driven by higher revenue. Over the last 3 years on average, earnings per share has increased by 40% per year but the company’s share price has only increased by 14% per year, which means it is significantly lagging earnings growth.

news.title: New major risk - Revenue and earnings growth
news.body: Earnings have declined by 22% per year over the past 5 years. This is considered a major risk. Ultimately, shareholders want to see a good return on their investment and that generally comes from sharing in the company's profits. If profits are declining over an extended period, then in most cases the share price will decline over time unless the company can turn around its fortunes. A trend of falling earnings can be very difficult to turn around. If the company is well already established it may also be a sign the company has matured and is in decline. In addition, if the company pays dividends it will also likely need to reduce or cut them, striking a dual blow to total shareholder returns. news.title: Third quarter 2026 earnings released: EPS: ₹0.41 (vs ₹1.25 in 3Q 2025)
news.body: Third quarter 2026 results: EPS: ₹0.41 (down from ₹1.25 in 3Q 2025). Revenue: ₹264.3m (up 24% from 3Q 2025). Net income: ₹2.07m (down 67% from 3Q 2025). Profit margin: 0.8% (down from 2.9% in 3Q 2025). The decrease in margin was driven by higher expenses. Over the last 3 years on average, earnings per share has increased by 13% per year whereas the company’s share price has increased by 14% per year.

news.title: New major risk - Share price stability
news.body: The company's share price has been highly volatile over the past 3 months. It is more volatile than 90% of Indian stocks, typically moving 8.5% a week. This is considered a major risk. Share price volatility increases the risk of potential losses in the short-term as the stock tends to have larger drops in price more frequently than other stocks. It may also indicate the stock is highly sensitive to market conditions or economic conditions rather than being sensitive to its own business performance, which may also be inconsistent.
